title: Financial Reporting Environment
description: Understand the purpose of financial reporting and who uses financial statements.
html:
What is financial reporting?

Financial reporting communicates financial information about a business to people who need that information to make decisions.

Who uses financial statements?

  • Investors
  • Lenders
  • Creditors
  • Management
  • Regulators

General-purpose financial reporting

General-purpose financial statements are designed primarily to provide useful financial information to external users.

Example

An investor considering buying stock in a company may review its financial statements to evaluate profitability, debt levels, cash flows and financial position.

Main idea

Financial reporting exists to provide useful information for economic decision-making.

quiz.prompt: Which user is considered an external user of financial statements?
quiz.explanation: Investors are external users because they are outside the company and use financial information to make investment decisions.
